int_name: N BROAD ST & W OLNEY AVE

result.summary: The image shows a wide commercial corridor with a marked zebra crosswalk and a central median refuge. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks and markings are present, the long crossing distance across multiple lanes of traffic creates a high-exposure environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic, increasing exposure time in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The large bus and parked vehicles can block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians at the crossing.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Slip Lane
hazards.description: A channelized right-turn lane allows vehicles to maintain higher speeds while crossing pedestrian paths.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon
interventions.description: Add active warning lights or a signal to control traffic and provide a protected crossing interval.

interventions.title: Slip Lane Modification
interventions.description: Reconstruct the slip lane with a tighter radius or eliminate it to slow turning vehicles and improve safety.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility crosswalks and pedestrian signals but requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic over a significant distance. The environment is primarily commercial with a transit hub, but lacks physical buffers like medians or curb extensions to protect vulnerable road users.
